rule: Call on a receiver of **unknown type**: `recv.member`, using the LAST receiver segment (`self.client.get()` → `client.get`; `a.b.c()` → `b.c`). | Call on a **computed receiver** (call result, index, literal, `super` when the superclass is not in the scan): `.member` — a leading dot means "receiver unknown". | **low**: a guess — receiver of unknown type (`recv.m`, `.m`), or a bare name not found in the scan. | **C4 Unresolved references are preserved.** A call the tool cannot resolve is still emitted as a low guess (`recv.m`, `.m`, a bare name). It is never dropped and never promoted to a resolved ID. | `this.x` assigned a value is a callback.
notes: `this.client.get()` -> `client.get` (the SPEC's own example: last receiver segment); `this.opts.retry.policy.apply()` -> `policy.apply`. `res.data.items[0].render()`: the receiver ends in an index -> computed `.render`. `makeThing()` / `notDefinedAnywhere()` are bare names not found in the scan -> low guesses that must still be emitted (C4). `makeThing().start()` and `"abc".toUpperCase()` have call-result / literal receivers -> `.start`, `.toUpperCase`. The '`this.x` assigned a value is a callback' rule covers calling `this.client` itself, not calling a member of it; `this.client` holds an untyped parameter, so its type is unknown.
